workflows.name: Research a Brand from Its Website
workflows.description: Paste a website and an agent researches the brand behind it: it opens the site with a browser, searches the web for what the site leaves out, and writes cited notes. An extractor turns the notes into a brand name, audience, voice, description and tagline that a brand kit can use. The researcher uses browser and web search tools. Pick a language model for the researcher and the extractor.
workflows.sourceId: nodetool-base/Research a Brand from Its Website

data.comment:
# 🔎 Research a Brand from Its Website

Paste a website and get research notes plus the five fields a brand kit needs: name, audience, voice, one-line description and tagline. Use it to start a brand kit from a site you do not know well.

**How it works:** "Website" fills the "Research brief" prompt. "Research agent (browser + web search)" runs with the browser and web_search tools, capped at 12 turns and $1.00. It opens the site, searches for what the site leaves out, and writes notes with sources that go to "Research notes". "Brand profile fields", an Extractor, reads the notes and fills "Brand name", "Audience", "Voice", "Brand description" and "Tagline", leaving a field empty when the notes mark it unconfirmed. Each model step uses your default language model, or the one you pick on the node.

**Try this:** Point "Website" at your own site, then edit any field before you generate assets from it.

data.name: website
data.description: The brand's website. The agent starts here.

data.prompt:
Research the brand behind this website: {{ WEBSITE }}

1. Open the website with the browser tool. Open one or two more pages from it if the home page is thin, such as About or Pricing.
2. Use web search once or twice for what the site does not say: who uses the product and how others describe the brand.
3. Write research notes in Markdown with these sections:

## Brand
The brand name exactly as the site writes it, and what it sells, in one or two sentences.

## Audience
Who it is for, as specifically as the evidence allows.

## Voice
Three adjectives for the tone of the site's copy, each with a short quote from the site that shows it.

## Tagline
The site's own tagline or headline if it has one. Otherwise propose one of at most six words and say it is proposed.

## Colors
The main brand colors you saw, as hex codes if the page exposes them.

## Sources
Every URL you used.

Use at most eight tool calls in total, then write the notes. If a page refuses to load, say so and move on. Write "Not confirmed" for anything you could not find. Do not invent facts.

data.system: You are a brand strategist doing desk research. You open pages and search before you write, quote the brand's own words where you can, and say plainly when something is not confirmed.

data.system_prompt:
Extract a brand profile from the research notes in <TEXT>.
- brand_name: the brand name exactly as written in the notes.
- audience: who the brand is for, one sentence.
- voice: the tone of voice as three adjectives and a short instruction, one sentence.
- brand_description: what the brand is and how it should feel, one sentence.
- tagline: the brand's own tagline, or the proposed one when the notes give no confirmed tagline, at most eight words.
Use only the notes. Leave any other field empty when the notes say it is not confirmed.

workflows.name: Brand Asset Generator
workflows.description: Turn a brand name and vibe into a whole social kit in one run: the graph fans out to two branches at once — a streamed gallery of four on-brand, text-overlaid social images (Instagram, LinkedIn, X, product launch) and a one-page brand brief (voice, palette, tagline options). Differentiator: structured multi-asset outputs from a single fan-out graph. Each model step uses your default model for its type, and the image steps are paid.

data.comment:
# 🏷️ Brand Asset Generator

From a brand name and vibe, produces a social kit in one run: four on-brand images with text overlays and a one-page brand brief. Use it to rough out a launch kit before design work.

**How it works:** The four inputs feed two branches. In the image branch, "5 Write image prompts" asks for four prompts (Instagram, LinkedIn, X, product launch), and "6 Split into 4 prompts" emits them one at a time. "7 Render each image" renders each at 1:1. "8 Stamp brand name" writes "1 Brand name" in "4 Brand color" at size 72, "9 Overlay tagline" adds "3 Tagline" in white at size 40, and "10 Collect gallery" gathers the four images. In the brief branch, "5 Write brief prompt" feeds "6 Draft brand brief", which writes voice, palette and tagline options. Pick a language model on "6 Split into 4 prompts" and "6 Draft brand brief", and an image model on "7 Render each image". Each image is a paid generation.

**Try this:** Change "4 Brand color" to a deep red such as #B3261E and see the brand name on all four images change color.

data.prompt:
You are an art director building a social-media image kit for a brand.

BRAND
Name: {{ brand_name }}
Positioning: {{ brand_description }}

TASK
Write 4 distinct text-to-image prompts, one per asset listed below. Every prompt must:
- describe a concrete scene, composition, lighting and color mood that fits the brand
- leave clear negative space in the upper or lower third for a headline and logo overlay
- be fully self-contained (never mention "the brand", "our", or the other prompts)
- read as one vivid, comma-separated sentence a text-to-image model can render

ASSETS (write one prompt for each, in this exact order)
1. Instagram square post, a hero product-in-context moment
2. LinkedIn banner, calm and professional, wide horizon
3. X / Twitter header, bold and energetic, high contrast
4. Product announcement, clean studio look on a seamless backdrop

OUTPUT
Return exactly 4 lines: one prompt per line, in order. No numbering, labels, quotes, or blank lines.

data.prompt:
Write a one-page brand brief for the brand below.

BRAND
Name: {{ brand_name }}
Positioning: {{ brand_description }}
Working tagline: {{ tagline }}

Produce Markdown with exactly these sections:
- **Voice & tone** — 3 adjectives, then one sentence on how the brand speaks.
- **Color palette** — a primary color plus 2 complementary colors as hex codes, each with a one-line usage note.
- **Tagline options** — 3 alternatives to the working tagline, in the brand's voice.
- **Do / Don't** — 2 bullets each, covering visuals and copy.

Keep the whole brief under 200 words. Output only the Markdown, with no preamble.

data.system: You are a senior brand strategist. You turn a short positioning line into a sharp, usable brand guideline. Commit to concrete choices: name real hex colors, write taglines a copywriter could ship, and keep voice, palette and rules internally consistent so the brand reads as one coherent identity.

workflows.name: Hook & Thumbnail Factory
workflows.description: One video topic in, a full thumbnail pack out: scroll-stopping hook lines plus a color-graded, ready-to-post thumbnail for each. The differentiator is the fan-out — one hook stream drives a whole gallery of matching images in a single run.

data.comment:
# 🎬 Hook & Thumbnail Factory

Give a video topic and audience. The graph writes scroll-stopping hook lines and, for each hook, a matching color-graded thumbnail, all from one run.

**How it works:** "Video topic", "Target audience" and "How many hooks" (4 by default) fill "Build hook brief". "Stream hooks" is a List Generator that emits one hook at a time, and "Hook ideas" previews each one. For every hook, "Build thumbnail prompt" combines it with the topic, "Generate thumbnail" renders a 16:9 image, and "Color grade for punch" raises contrast to 1.18 and brightness by 0.03. "Latest thumbnail" previews each image and "Collect gallery" gathers them into "Thumbnail gallery". Pick a text model on "Stream hooks" and an image model on "Generate thumbnail". Each thumbnail is one paid image.

**Try this:** Set "How many hooks" to 2 for a cheaper test run, then raise "contrast" on "Color grade for punch" to 1.35 and compare how much the thumbnails pop.

data.description: How many hook lines (and thumbnails) to produce. Each thumbnail is one FLUX image, so higher counts cost and take proportionally longer.

data.prompt:
You are a short-form video strategist. Write exactly {{ count }} scroll-stopping hook lines for a video.

TOPIC: {{ topic }}
AUDIENCE: {{ audience }}

Rules:
- Each hook is a single line, spoken in the first 2 seconds.
- Lead with curiosity, a bold claim, or a relatable pain the audience feels.
- No clickbait the video can't pay off; no emojis; no numbering.
- Keep each hook under 12 words so it fits on screen.

Output format: return the {{ count }} hooks as a plain list, one hook per line, nothing else.
